source.title: Researchers develop AI model that maps how genes work together in human cells
source.author: The Mount Sinai Hospital

athena.directive: Establish a self-sovereign, integrated bioinformatics and biomedical research intelligence layer within the Creative Liberation Engine, leveraging contextual AI models like GSFM to map gene interactions and drive novel scientific discovery.
athena.rationale: The development of AI models that understand gene function through context, analogous to large language models, represents a significant advancement in biology. Integrating such a capability aligns with the Creative Liberation Engine's constitutional mandate for self-owned, advanced AI solutions (Article I). This will enable the Creative Liberation Engine to interpret complex biological datasets, identify disease mechanisms, and propose new therapeutic targets, thereby extending its intelligence into critical scientific domains and ensuring a 'complete implementation' (Article IX) of cutting-edge AI for research.

options.title: Integrated Biomedical Research Workbench
options.description: Develop a dedicated, comprehensive workbench within the Creative Liberation Engine for bioinformatics research. This would encompass a full lifecycle from data ingestion to advanced visualization and interpretation of GSFM-derived insights.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant initial investment in specialized data pipelines for biological data (e.g., gene sets, multi-omics), distributed training infrastructure for GSFM-like models, and complex UI/UX for interactive biological visualizations. High development complexity due to the specialized domain.
options.architecture: A new microservice or agent (e.g., 'BIO-GENESIS' agent) dedicated to GSFM operations. Robust data ingestion pipelines capable of handling diverse public and proprietary gene set data. A distributed training framework optimized for GSFM model architectures. A GraphQL API for querying gene relationships, functional annotations, and disease associations. Integration with KEEPER for structured storage of learned biological patterns and insights. Scalable compute for both training and inference tasks. Secure data governance and privacy protocols for sensitive biological information.
options.design: A highly interactive and modular web-based workbench. Key visualizations would include dynamic, force-directed gene-gene interaction networks, customizable heatmaps for gene expression patterns across various biological contexts, and an 'Explainable AI' panel. This panel would leverage an integrated LLM to generate natural language explanations of gene functions and disease implications based on GSFM outputs. Users would have drill-down capabilities into specific genes, filters for biological processes, and the ability to save custom gene sets. A 'contextual discovery' UI element would allow users to input a gene set and receive suggestions for related biological contexts and potential functions.

options.title: Gene Oracle API for Scientific Discovery
options.description: Focus primarily on exposing GSFM's capabilities as a highly optimized API service, allowing other Creative Liberation Engine agents or external systems to query for gene relationships and functions.
options.tradeoffs: While providing broad utility through integration, this approach offers limited direct user interaction and visualization within the Creative Liberation Engine itself. The quality of insight consumption and visualization would depend on integrating applications.
options.architecture: A highly optimized GSFM inference service exposed via a RESTful API. The API would accept gene lists (or identifiers) and return predicted functions, disease associations, and related gene sets with associated confidence scores. Data ingestion and model retraining would be an internally managed, scheduled process, separate from the public-facing API. Emphasis on high throughput and low latency for inference queries. Minimal internal UI beyond API monitoring and management.
options.design: A minimalist API documentation portal, potentially using tools like Swagger UI, with clear, interactive examples of API calls and expected responses. The focus would be on developer experience, clarity, and ease of integration for other Creative Liberation Engine agents or external research tools. No dedicated front-end for deep biological exploration; visualizations would be left to the integrating applications, though the API could provide structured data suitable for common graph visualization libraries.

options.title: Contextual Gene Search & Recommendation Engine
options.description: Integrate GSFM's contextual understanding into KEEPER to enhance semantic search and recommendation capabilities for biological entities and processes.
options.tradeoffs: This option is tightly coupled with KEEPER's existing architecture, which might limit the standalone capabilities of the bioinformatics intelligence. It could also require significant re-engineering of KEEPER's core search indexing and retrieval mechanisms.
options.architecture: The GSFM model would act as a backend for a semantic search and recommendation engine, primarily integrated within KEEPER. Gene sets and biological queries would be embedded into a common vector space, allowing for contextual similarity searches. When users query for biological processes or disease terms, the engine would leverage GSFM embeddings to retrieve relevant genes and their contextual functions. It would also recommend related research papers, datasets, or Creative Liberation Engine internal knowledge based on gene set similarity and GSFM insights.
options.design: Enhance KEEPER's search interface with new 'biological context' filters and a 'related genes/pathways' recommendation sidebar. Search results for individual genes would include a 'contextual summary' generated by an integrated LLM, explaining the gene's known roles in different cellular environments, directly drawing from GSFM insights. Visualizations would be integrated directly into search results, potentially showing mini-network diagrams or enrichment plots to quickly convey relationships and contexts.

options.title: Autonomous Biomedical Hypothesis Generator
options.description: Extend the GSFM with an agent-based system that autonomously generates and validates novel hypotheses about gene functions or disease mechanisms.
options.tradeoffs: High complexity in building robust validation and hypothesis generation agents. There is an inherent risk of generating unsubstantiated or incorrect hypotheses without extremely careful tuning, extensive validation, and continuous refinement.
options.architecture: An agent-based system (e.g., AURORA for hypothesis formulation, VERA for validation) would operate on top of the GSFM. The GSFM would identify novel or unexpected gene relationships and contextual shifts. An LLM agent would then generate plausible biological hypotheses based on these GSFM insights. VERA would be responsible for validating these hypotheses against existing scientific literature, public databases, or simulated biological data. A continuous feedback loop would be established to refine both the GSFM and the hypothesis generation/validation agents.
options.design: A dedicated 'Hypothesis Dashboard' within the Creative Liberation Engine. This dashboard would display autonomously generated hypotheses, along with their supporting evidence (e.g., GSFM outputs, relevant literature citations, validation scores). Users would be able to review, refine, and prioritize hypotheses. Visualizations would focus on the evidence chain and the contextual shifts that led to a particular hypothesis, perhaps showing how a gene's role or interactions change across different disease states or experimental conditions, thereby illustrating the basis of the new hypothesis.

options.title: Internal Collaborative Research Tool
options.description: Develop an internal collaborative tool for Creative Liberation Engine agents (and human operators) to explore, annotate, and refine GSFM-derived biological insights.
options.tradeoffs: Requires robust access control, versioning, and conflict resolution mechanisms for collaborative editing. Designing effective agent-human collaboration interfaces, especially for complex biological data, can be highly challenging.
options.architecture: A shared, version-controlled workspace integrated with KEEPER for tracking collaborative discoveries and annotations. This would include a secure user/agent authentication system. Data manipulation and annotation functionalities would be exposed through APIs, allowing different agents to interact with the same underlying biological data. A robust auditing and logging system would track all changes and contributions. Integration with internal communication channels for real-time collaboration.
options.design: A collaborative 'whiteboard' or 'canvas' interface where agents and human operators can visually manipulate gene sets, draw connections between biological entities, and add annotations. Real-time updates and multi-user cursors would facilitate simultaneous interaction. A structured commenting and review system would enable asynchronous feedback. Visualizations would be highly customizable, allowing different agents or operators to display and interact with biological data in their preferred formats while maintaining a common, underlying data model and understanding.
